Senses.Explanation: A dead teaching is a fixed formulation applied without the live responsiveness the records demand. Masters use the verdict for inherited understanding, formulaic words, and even a stick or phrase when someone clings to it as a settled way to receive people. Juelang Daosheng condemns teachers who receive people with dead words and dead teaching, comparing it to forcing an ox’s head down to eat grass. The Treatise on Tempering Chan says people cling to dead teaching and will not extend a hand at the precipice, even when they possess ability. Tianru Weize says even an understanding that agrees with buddhas and patriarchs remains dead teaching when it lacks “living intent”; the text itself supplies the dead/live contrast. Guxue Zhe says that clinging to a single use of the stick would itself become dead teaching, then lists his differing responses to different people. The headword therefore marks fixation, not a permanent class of forbidden words.
